items.title: NEW — where the `context` clause sits on a `fun` DECLARATION: after the return type (`fun f(): i32 context settings`, contexts.md §3's deliberate choice — the type grammar's own `context` suffix parses greedily and the declaration peels it back off) or after the parameters and BEFORE the `:` of the return type (`fun f() context settings: i32`). The greedy-peel reading has one real hole: a closure-typed return with its OWN clause — `fun f(): (\|\| void) context c` — cannot say whether `c` is the function's requirement or the returned closure's clause (the peel takes it for the function); the before-the-colon form spells both (`fun f() context c: (\|\| void) context d`). And whichever position stands, the TextMate grammar highlights `context` only after a `)` (`(?<=\))\s+(context)\b` — the closure-type rule), so on `fun f(): i32 context settings` the keyword paints as an identifier; the estate writes the declaration form at 0 std / 1 kolt / 2 docs sites against 30 closure-type clauses in std, so a move costs little today
items.discussion: the owner's ask (2026-09-14): 'File an item for whether or not the `context` clause on a `fun` declaration should be after the return type or after the parameters but before the `:` marker of the return type. If the current setup is best (after the return type), please note that the syntax highlighting doesn't recognize the keyword correctly.' REC: keep the position (it reads as the closure type's own clause, one spelling for one idea, and contexts.md §3 chose it knowingly), REFUSE the ambiguous closure-typed-return-with-clause form with a steer to parenthesize the return type (`fun f(): ((\|\| void) context d) context c`), and FIX the highlighter — the lookbehind admits any type-ending token (`)`, an identifier, `>`, `]`) so the declaration form paints, with a scope pin for both forms
items.body: Either way: a grammar_sync scope pin for `fun f(): i32 context settings` and `fun g(): (\|\| void) context c`; if the position moves: parser (`parse_function`'s head), formatter, the docs' every declaration example, the 3 estate sites, contexts.md §3 rewritten, a curated refusal for the old position with the rewrite as a quick fix; if it stays: the parenthesized-return refusal (one row) + the TextMate lookbehind + the book theme's copy.
